chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Sophisticated Lady recorded by many soloists
summary: He says it was recorded perhaps twenty-five times in solo versions, including Shorty Baker's.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: How many times would you --- say that 'Sophisticated Lady' was recorded?
Well, offhandedly, I would say even as many 20 or maybe 25.
That's by Duke and the band.
By different members of the band, different interpretations, different renditions of it.
And it became a solo vehicle for you, for Johnny Hodges, for Willie Smith, for Harry Carney and for anybody else?
Ah, Blanton and well almost everybody that was soloing, made some sort of a record of 'Sophisticated Lady.'
And you were saying that there were take-offs from portion of it, by whom?

I remember that the saxophone section made a take-off, what I call it, where "Sophisticated Lady" was the basic solo, but like harmonic melodies taken off from the original and things like that. I remember several of those were done. All this is getting kind of old to me because I haven't been with the band for seven years now. And that's a long time to remember the exact things that happened.
You said Shorty Baker did something?
Shorty Baker did a very fine solo rendition that I would call a take-off of "Sophisticated Lady"
On a number called something else? Or --
No just his -- like his interpretation.
I see his solo improvisation on --
